gaps: Primary source for every record is the LLBC 'British Columbia Executive Council Appointments 1871-1986' (execouncil.pdf, pp. 32-50, saved as raw/llbc_execouncil_1871-1986.pdf). The Wikipedia '<Premier> ministry' articles (raw/wiki_*.wikitext) cite the same document and were used only as a cross-check.

Portfolio titles follow LLBC's short forms ('Lands and Works', 'Finance and Agriculture', 'Attorney-General') expanded to 'Minister of ...' / 'Chief Commissioner of ...'. The 'Chief Commissioner' titles for Lands and Works (to 22 Dec 1908) and Lands (22 Dec 1908 to 1 Mar 1911) are from LLBC footnotes and Wikipedia's McBride note. The 'Minister of' prefix on other titles was not checked against the Gazette.

Provincial Secretary and Minister of Education were held together to 1918 (LLBC shows them as one combined 'Provincial Secretary/Education' post). They are recorded as two parallel records per holder.

Vacancies without a holder: Lands and Works 23-31 Dec 1906; Lands 21 Oct-1 Nov 1909; President of the Council 25 Sep-Nov 1913 and 4-8 Jun 1903; Finance 12-15 Feb 1917; Labour 28 Jan-12 Apr 1922; Public Works 24-28 Jan 1922; Industries 28 Aug-6 Sep 1924; Mines 2-7 Mar 1928; Industries 21 Aug-5 Sep 1928; Labour 21-30 Aug 1928; Public Works 28 Jun-15 Jul 1933; Mines 2-5 Jun 1933; Industries 15 Nov-1 Dec 1933; Trade and Industry 10-23 Dec 1937; Attorney-General 19-24 Nov 1941.
Oliver-to-MacLean transition: the ministers were not re-sworn, and LLBC leaves a 3-day gap (17-20 Aug 1927) between the two ministries.
Skipped ministers without portfolio: Mary Ellen Smith (Oliver, 24 Mar-19 Nov 1921) and Royal Lethington Maitland (Tolmie, 21 Aug 1928 to [15 Nov 1933]).
Party is the governing party of the ministry. For W.M. Dennies and William Savage (non-MLA 'union government' appointees, 1933) it is null because LLBC does not state a party.

Wikipedia errors found and overridden by LLBC: Tolmie ministry gives Agriculture Jun-Nov 1933 to Frank Putnam (LLBC: Tolmie himself), prints Lougheed's Public Works start as 15 Nov 1933 (LLBC: 21 Aug 1928), and spells 'Hinchcliffe' (LLBC: Hinchliffe). Oliver ministry omits Oliver as President of the Council. Brewster ministry omits Farris's acting AG period (14-23 May 1917) and ends Ralph Smith on 15 Feb 1917 (LLBC: died 12 Feb). Small date differences: Sutherland Mines 2 vs 7 Mar 1928, Howe Mines 2 vs 5 Jun 1933, Tatlow Lands and Works 23 vs 31 Dec 1906.
